findings.title: Negative offset on a prev cursor reaches Django slicing and raises
findings.body: In BasePaginator.get_result, `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` passes a negative offset straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` when `cursor.is_prev` is true. Django rejects negative slice indexes with ValueError, so a crafted or stale `prev` cursor with a negative offset turns into a 500 on every paginated endpoint that uses DateTimePaginator. The same applies to the new OptimizedCursorPaginator path.

findings.title: Next-page negative offsets are silently clamped to 0, returning wrong rows
findings.body: For non-prev cursors, `max(0, offset)` silently replaces a negative offset with 0. The cursor's offset is ignored, so the client gets the first page of results instead of the page it asked for, and the returned next/prev cursors do not match the page actually served. Before this change the request was rejected or errored; now it returns misleading data. The `extra`/`len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check at line ~192 also still uses the unclamped `offset`, so the two values disagree.

findings.title: Advanced-feature negative-offset branch slices with a negative start index
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with `start_offset = cursor.offset` (negative). Django raises ValueError for negative indexing, so the branch always fails. It is reachable from the request path because the endpoint sets `enable_advanced_features=True` for superusers and global-access members who pass `optimized_pagination=true` and supply a cursor with a negative offset.

findings.title: Privilege gate comment claims permissions are enforced at queryset level, which is false
findings.body: The comment says negative offsets are 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level' and that the branch 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds'. The queryset is built identically in both branches, filtered only by organization and the request's filters, so no extra permission check is applied here. The 'advanced' behavior is just an alternate offset handling that is gated on superuser/global access. Relying on a misleading safety comment for a privilege boundary invites future mistakes.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result with divergent logic
findings.body: The new class copies almost all of BasePaginator.get_result, including the prev-cursor handling, and then diverges (the negative-offset branch and the `offset` vs `start_offset` mismatch). The two implementations now differ in subtle ways, so fixes to one (such as the clamping change in BasePaginator) will not reach the other. The class also changes no pagination semantics for the default path, so it adds maintenance risk without a clear benefit.

findings.title: organization_context.member may be None, causing AttributeError for non-superusers
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` dereferences `member` for any non-superuser. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is optional, and OrganizationAuditPermission can admit users without a member record, so this line can raise AttributeError and return a 500 for those callers. The check should guard against a missing member.

findings.title: Undocumented, unversioned query flag switches the pagination implementation
findings.body: The `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter changes which paginator runs and enables negative-offset cursors, but it is not part of the serializer, not documented, and not covered by any test. Clients can pass it arbitrarily, and the behavior is effectively an unreviewed API surface on an EXPERIMENTAL endpoint.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are allowed, but the code does not support them
findings.body: The comment says Cursor offsets are allowed to be negative to enable reverse pagination, but Cursor performs no validation and the paginators either clamp (BasePaginator) or fail on slicing (OptimizedCursorPaginator) negative offsets. The comment describes a feature that does not work and will mislead maintainers.

findings.title: No tests added for changed pagination behavior or new paginator
findings.body: The PR changes shared pagination behavior in BasePaginator (affecting every DateTimePaginator user), adds a new OptimizedCursorPaginator class, and adds a new endpoint code path, but includes no tests. Negative-offset cursors, the superuser gate, and the optimized_pagination path are all untested, and the regressions described above would not be caught.

findings.title: PR description is placeholder text
findings.body: The description reads only 'Test 1' and gives no motivation, behavior change, or risk assessment for changing shared pagination semantics. Reviewers cannot tell what behavior is intended or why negative offsets are needed.
